subject: Certificate boundary & resolver stewardship — onboarding questions
messages:
From: Alice Mann <alice.mann@acme-fin.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Certificate boundary & resolver stewardship — onboarding questions

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. A few follow-ups from our security team as we scope the private (VPC/on-prem) deployment:

1) Proof-of-origin for private FQDNs: our infosec needs a lightweight, auditable way to accept that an incoming CSR or presented cert is legitimately associated with Acme's private namespace. We don't want to hand over private CA keys. Common asks: signed LOA, DNS TXT ownership proof (within our split-horizon), or a short-lived JWT exchanged via a pre-established API. What patterns has Redwood been operating with for customers that keep their own resolvers?

2) Resolver stewardship: who owns the resolver authoritative answers for private-hosted names? We have split-horizon today and would prefer to keep control, but want Redwood's recommendations for minimizing client-side complexity (e.g., stub resolvers, conditional forwarders, or using an internal forwarder hosted in our VPC).

3) Termination boundary: we need clarity on where TLS terminates in Redwood's private deployment: at an edge adapter inside our VPC, at a customer-side proxy, or at a Redwood-managed sidecar. For mutual TLS (mTLS) use cases, perf and certificate rotation are big concerns.

4) OCSP / stapling + rotation: our compliance team wants an SLA for revocation checks (OCSP stapling supported? fallback behavior?). Also interested in recommended rotation cadence for short-lived intermediate certs versus long-lived root anchors.

Can you share a short runbook or checklist (templates are fine) that we can hand to ops and legal? We may need a signed LOA template for our change board.

Thanks — happy to sync if easier.

- Alice
Security Architect
Acme Financial Services
[Attachment: acme-onboard-questions.pdf (pdf)]
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Mann <alice.mann@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Certificate boundary & resolver stewardship — onboarding questions

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of patterns we've used on private deployments and a proposed path forward for Acme. Attached two short artifacts: csr-proof-playbook.pdf and resolver-stewardship-checklist.xlsx.

High-level recommendations (TL;DR):
- Namespace ownership: customer retains authoritative control over private namespace. Redwood accepts either a CSR signed by the customer's internal CA (cross-signed where required) or a CSR accompanied by a signed LOA + DNS TXT proof from the customer's split-horizon resolver. We prefer DNS TXT when customers can manage records; it's automated and auditable.
- Proof methods (ordered by friction):
  1) DNS TXT under private zone (preferred when split-horizon makes TXT reachable from Redwood's validation agent inside the customer's VPC).
  2) Signed LOA (template attached) + short-lived API bearer token exchange (we provide a one-time provisioning flow).
  3) Internal CA cross-sign / shared root (only for highly regulated on-prem where customer does not permit automated checks).
- Resolver stewardship: customer-managed authoritative resolver is recommended. For simpler client routing we offer an optional Redwood forwarder deployed in your VPC (container) that forwards unknown queries to your internal resolver. That forwarder runs as a non-authoritative stub/forwarder and is covered by our SLA when hosted in the customer's VPC.
- TLS termination boundary options:
  * Edge adapter in-customer VPC (Redwood-managed container): TLS terminates at the adapter; backend connections to our runtime use mTLS. Pros: customer keeps private certs; simpler firewall policy.
  * Customer proxy termination: your infra terminates TLS and forwards to Redwood over a private link — you retain full control but manage rotation.
  * Sidecar model: lightweight sidecar on host that handles private certs; useful for air-gapped installs.
  We'll help you size pros/cons; our standard is to terminate at the Edge adapter in most Dedicated/Private installs.
- OCSP/Stapling + rotation: we support OCSP stapling for public-interfacing certificates. For private certs we recommend short-lived intermediates (7–14 days) and a pinned root anchor rotation process. Redwood exposes certificate rotation events and logs via the Console (audit stream) and can emit syslog/CloudWatch events to your collector.

Next steps:
1) If you can confirm which proof method you prefer (DNS TXT vs LOA vs cross-sign), we'll produce a step-by-step validation playbook and a CSR submission endpoint.
2) If you want us to host the forwarder in your VPC, we'll kick off a short infra ticket (access, CIDR, service account).
3) Legal: I'll attach the LOA template and a short statement-of-responsibility you can sign.

Attaching: csr-proof-playbook.pdf; resolver-stewardship-checklist.xlsx

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min ops walk-through.

—Olga
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: csr-proof-playbook.pdf]
[Attachment: resolver-stewardship-checklist.xlsx]

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2028 08:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Certificate boundary & resolver stewardship — onboarding questions

Thanks Olga — great summary. Two clarifications from compliance/ops perspective: 

1) OCSP: for the internal/private cert case we recommend stapling only if the cert issuer supports OCSP responders reachable from the customer environment. If not, our fallback is a short-lived intermediate + revocation list pushed to the edge forwarder. We log all revocation events and retain them per the customer's retention policy.

2) Wildcards & SANs: we discourage broad wildcard certs for private namespaces. Recommend explicit SAN lists per service to keep auditability and limit blast radius. If Acme requires service-level wildcarding, we'll need a separate risk sign-off and shorter TTL for rotation.

I've added a brief note in the onboarding drive (link below) describing the audit artefacts we will produce (certificate issuance log, rotation events, OCSP logs, and resolver TTL snapshots). Legal has requested the LOA be explicit about namespace scope and rotation ownership; Olga, can you add a one-paragraph statement in the LOA template that calls out rotation cadence and who is permitted to request revocation?

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-onboarding

—Laura
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Olga / Laura — this all looks reasonable. We prefer the DNS TXT validation flow (we control split-horizon and can create ephemeral TXT records from our staging resolver). We'll also take Redwood's forwarder inside our VPC for simplicity.

Two asks before we proceed: 
- Please send the LOA template with the additional rotation/responsibility paragraph Laura requested.
- Can you provide the short script or command that the forwarder will run to perform the TXT check so our ops team can validate in staging?

I've attached a completed, redacted change board form that lists the namespace and contact points — legal will need the LOA signed but wants to review your rotation paragraph first.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

- Alice
